en: O Nandagopa, that meditation born in your house, produced from the womb of Yaśodā—
I, dwelling on the Vindhya mountains, shall destroy both of them.
The Hymn to the Auspicious Mother Vindhyavāsinī
I worship the dweller of the Vindhya mountains, the crusher of Niśumbha and Śumbha, the shatterer of fierce Muṇḍa, who shines forth in the forest and in battle. (1)
I worship the dweller of the Vindhya mountains, who bears a trident and a severed head, who removes the afflictions of the earth, and who resides in every single home. ||2||
I worship the Goddess who dwells in the Vindhya mountains, who removes the suffering of the poor, who bestows abundant prosperity, and who takes away the grief of separation.
I worship the dweller of the Vindhya mountains, who possesses eyes that are tremulous with playful grace, who is a creeper-like vine bestowing boons, and who bears a skull and a trident. ||4||
I worship Vindhyavāsinī, who holds the *mudrā* of the *gada* (club) in her hand, who bestows auspiciousness upon Śiva, who is most excellent, fair-faced, and beautiful. ||5||
I worship the dweller of the Vindhya mountains, who bestows boons upon the sages, who assumes a threefold form, and who resides both in water and on land.
I worship the dweller of the Vindhya mountains, who brings about a distinguished creation, who assumes a vast form, and who sports within the great belly [of Brahmā]. ||7||
I worship the Goddess who dwells in the Vindhya mountains, who is served by Indra and others, who shatters the lineage of Mura and his kin, and who brings about pure intelligence. ||8||
